claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 29-35: `public async Task<Order> CancelOrderAsync(int orderId)` / `{` / `var order = await repository.FindAsync(orderId)` / `?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"order {orderId} not found");` / blank / `order.Status = "cancelled";` / `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();`. The `??` is on the method's first statement; the assignment is three lines later and nothing between them reads `order.Status`. The lesson's block reproduces those seven lines character-for-character (whitespace normalised).

The whole method (29-38) never reads `order.Status`: it assigns `order.Status = "cancelled"` unconditionally at line 34, with no `if`/`switch` anywhere in OrderService.cs. ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs catches only KeyNotFoundException(404), ArgumentException(400), Exception(500) — the app has no 409 path at all. Confirmed again this round by reading both files at stage-1; the shipped-order cancellation was executed live in round 1 (order 2, `shipped` -> 200 OK, row restored).

Re-run live this session (lab up: donhang-api/db/web): token from POST /api/v1/auth/login (anh.tran@example.com), then `curl -sS -i -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/99999/cancel -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` -> `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found` and body `{"title":"Not found","status":404,"detail":"order 99999 not found"}` — byte-identical to §2 and §7. Path: middleware `catch (KeyNotFoundException ex)` -> `WriteProblemAsync(context, StatusCodes.Status404NotFound, "Not found", ex.Message)`.

refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt:7543-7546 verbatim: "The 400 (Bad Request) status code indicates that the server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, or deceptive request routing)." All three examples are defects of the request message itself, matching the claim's "in the request itself".

refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt:7589-7591 verbatim: "The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists." The claim reproduces both halves. (Lines 7591-7594 add the 410 preference clause, which the lesson no longer touches after the round-1 q6 rewrite.)

refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt:7652-7654 verbatim: "The 409 (Conflict) status code indicates that the request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource." Same section continues "This code is used in situations where the user might be able to resolve the conflict and resubmit the request", which the lesson's shipped-order framing does not contradict.

DonHang.Domain/IOrderRepository.cs:7 @ stage-1: `Task<Order?> FindAsync(int id);`. The only implementation, EfOrderRepository.cs:9-10, is `db.Orders.Include(o => o.Items).FirstOrDefaultAsync(o => o.Id == id)` — FirstOrDefaultAsync yields null for no match rather than throwing. Live confirmation that null becomes KeyNotFoundException and not a 500: PATCH /api/v1/orders/-5/cancel (authenticated) -> 404 `{"title":"Not found",...,"detail":"order -5 not found"}`.

No rfc9457 mirror exists under refs/rfc (only 6265/9110/9111/9112), so this was fetched from www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457(.txt). §3.1 introduces the list as "Problem detail objects can have the following members" and names type, status, title, detail, instance; the definitions seen are "The 'title' member is a JSON string containing a short, human-readable summary of the problem type" and "The 'status' member is a JSON number indicating the HTTP status code...". No sentence stating the members "are all optional" was returned — "can have" is the strongest wording seen.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: RFC 9457 §3.1: "Problem detail objects can have the following members" — type, status, title, detail, instance; none is marked required. Đơn Hàng's WriteProblemAsync fills exactly title/status/detail, which is this app's choice, not a requirement of the format.

issues.text: The prose promises each status box names an endpoint, but node G names none — it names the absence of a check. Node C also invents a route: the app has no `POST /orders`; it is `POST /api/v1/orders` (`[Route("api/v1/orders")]` + `[HttpPost]` in OrdersController), and node E already uses the `.../` elision style for exactly this reason.
issues.quote: the diagram's three status boxes each name which endpoint illustrates them … C[400 - POST /orders] … G[409 - nothing checks this yet]
issues.fix: Write node C as `C[400 - POST .../orders]` to match E's elision, and make the prose exact: "the diagram's `400` and `404` boxes name the endpoint that illustrates each; the `409` box names the check that is missing."

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and the list reads as a lifecycle. The four values are real — db/schema.sql @ stage-1 has `CHECK (status IN ('new', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled'))` and seed.sql uses all four — but no claim in the ledger covers them. "then `"cancelled"`" implies cancellation follows shipping, which §5 then contradicts: a `"new"` or `"paid"` order is cancelled the same way.
issues.quote: Every order carries a `status` — `"new"`, `"paid"`, `"shipped"`, then `"cancelled"` — and cancelling one that's already `"shipped"`
issues.fix: Drop the implied sequence: "Every order carries a `status` — one of `"new"`, `"paid"`, `"shipped"`, `"cancelled"` — and cancelling one that's already `"shipped"`…". Add a claim to `.meta.json` with `source_hint` "examples/don-hang @ stage-1: db/schema.sql:22-23 — CHECK (status IN ('new','paid','shipped','cancelled'))".

issues.text: "never `400`" is stated as a rule of HTTP, and no claim covers it. RFC 9110 §15.5.1 leaves 400 to "something that is perceived to be a client error", so a server that validates the id before looking it up may legitimately answer 400. What is verifiable is this app: live, authenticated `PATCH /api/v1/orders/-5/cancel` -> 404, body `{"title":"Not found","status":404,"detail":"order -5 not found"}`.
issues.quote: as long as it's a value the route accepts, a lookup that finds nothing is still `404`, never `400`
issues.fix: Bind it to this app: "…as long as it's a value the route accepts, `CancelOrderAsync` just looks it up, and a lookup that finds nothing answers `404` — the request's shape was fine, so only the id was missing." Add a `behavior` claim citing the live `-5` result.

issues.text: The sentence omits the condition the result depends on. `OrdersController.Cancel` carries `[Authorize]`; without a token the same request answers `401` with an empty body, not `404` (verified live this session). Claim 3 in the ledger says "authenticated PATCH"; §2 drops that word, and §7 only supplies the token two sections later.
issues.quote: Sending `PATCH /api/v1/orders/99999/cancel` gets `404` with `{"title":"Not found","status":404,"detail":"order 99999 not found"}`.
issues.fix: Add the condition inline: "Sending `PATCH /api/v1/orders/99999/cancel` as a signed-in customer gets `404` with `{…}`."
